title: Jam City 将裁员约 60 人
content:
Jam City to cut around 60 staff – Mobilegamer.biz
Skip to content
Harry Potter: Hogwarts Mystery maker Jam City is to cut around 60 staff, we can confirm.
In a
LinkedIn post
the firm said it would be cutting its workforce by about 10%; a spokesperson later confirmed that around 60 staff would be leaving the company.
The statement in full reads: “Today is a difficult day for our Jam City teams. We’ve made the decision to reduce our workforce by approximately 10%, impacting colleagues across the company. No studios or games will be closed as a result.”
“We’ve worked hard to improve game performance and strengthen our business. While we’ve made progress, further changes are necessary to build a more sustainable future for Jam City. We understand the profound impact this decision has on our colleagues and their families.”
“To those leaving Jam City, your creativity and talent have helped bring our games to millions of players and we are grateful. Thank you for being a part of our City and for everything you’ve helped us build.”
The LA-based developer
bid farewell to cofounder and CEO Joshua Yguado
earlier this year after 16 years at the helm. Former Netmarble US boss Chul-min Sim replaced him as CEO, and continues to also serve as CEO of Kabam. Both Kabam and Jam City are subsidiaries of Korean giant Netmarble.
Jam City also sold off Jurassic World: Alive maker Ludia
to a group of Canadian investors in 2025 after several rounds of layoffs. It acquired the Canadian developer in 2021 for $165m.
